The study "Online Facilitation of Field Instruction for the Social Work Programs of UP Open University" by Finaflor F. Taylan and Paula Grace Muyco investigates the effectiveness of online facilitation for field instruction (FI) within the Diploma in/Master of Social Work (D/MSW) program at the University of the Philippines Open University (UPOU). The researchers addressed a gap in research regarding clinical preparation in programs where internships are facilitated online, which is significant for UPOU students who are geographically dispersed.

Using a qualitative design and thematic analysis, the researchers analyzed 12 final sharing outputs from the 2016-2017 academic year. The study utilized Kolb and Fry’s (1974) Experiential Learning Cycle as a theoretical framework. Findings revealed that students successfully navigated all four stages of the cycle. During the concrete experience stage, students provided detailed accounts of agency profiles and activities. In the reflective observation stage, students identified challenges like emotional struggles and managing responsibilities, which led to realizations regarding professional competencies and the application of theory to practice. In the abstract conceptualization stage, students reported gaining technical knowledge and life skills. Finally, in the active experimentation stage, students provided recommendations for agencies and the program.

The authors conclude that online facilitation is effective, as the open and distance e-learning framework allowed students to maximize experiential learning and integrate theory and practice through guided reflection.
